4.text: RAILWAY CENTRAL P U B L I C R E A L M PROJECT TYPE: Competition SCALE: Large (100,000 - 999,999 m2) YORK, ENGLAND, UK TIME: June 2024- July 2024 PROJECT ROLE: Junior Landscape Designer GIS site analysis, Landscape masterplan, 3D modelling, Diagrams, CGI rendering RAILWAY CENTRAL LANDSCAPE DESIGN A two-site entry landscape competition for a new masterplan in front of a central railway station in the historic city - York, reimagining a disused industrial rail landscape as a connected public realm. The proposal comprises Central Park, a green and blue civic landscape reconnecting neighbourhoods and nature, and Coal Drops Plaza, a robust public space celebrating railway and industrial heritage. Existing rails, materials, and spontaneous vegetation are retained and reinterpreted to shape identity and circulation, with strong north–south connections transforming historic linear rail movement into a multidirectional, people-led landscape.

8.text: ? ? The History Of The Site Since the 17th century, the area was dedicated to hosting crops and agricultural fields, as York's expansion was confined within the walls. The productive landscape surrounded the town on all sides. During the industrial age, the area became the biggest railway yard in the city, leading to the construction of the new and third Central Station just outside the city walls The site is currently a brownfield, unused and inaccessible to the public. It acts as a significant barrier, dividing the urban fabric and lacking function and purpose. With the new development and approved masterplan, the area will undergo a transformation, being revitalized and a significant portion returned to nature and the community. The site holds a rich historical significance. To effectively develop and revitalize it, it is essential to first understand its past and the transformations it has undergone over time, shaping it into its current state. Its prosperous history of productivity should be respected and celebrated in the design, bringing to life the traces that still endure today. DESIGN CONCEPT 1850 1890 2024 2026

9.text: TRACING THE PAST: THE AGRICULTURAL FIELDS There are no traces of the previous agricultural structures in the urban fabric or road layout. We have chosen to rediscover and celebrate this hidden and forgotten pattern of a productive landscape by reintroducing it in the new scheme. 0 25 50 100m The site was historically a busy railway yard, defined by dense, linear tracks that shaped movement and production. To honour this character, we aim to preserve existing rails where possible and retrace former tracks to guide the park’s design and visitor circulation. TRACING THE PAST: THE RAILWAYS 0 25 50 100m TRACING THE EXISTING Though now disused, the site retains traces of its past as vegetation reclaims the tracks and concrete. We aim to embrace this natural takeover, reuse on-site materials such as the ballast gravel used for tracks or crushed concrete from demolitions, and retain existing planting wherever possible. 0 25 50 100m While honouring the past, the design also looks forward. Strong north– south connections will shape the park, linking neighbourhoods and supporting comfortable movement. CONNECTING 0 25 50 100m ACTIVATING Considering the land use of the masterplan and the park's edge conditions, we have also examined where and how to strategically place activation and attractor points to ensure the park becomes a successful destination. 0 25 50 100m BRING BACK WHAT WAS THERE GIVE NEW LIFE TO WHAT IS THERE

30.text: PROJECT TYPE: Competition SCALE: Medium (1,000 - 99,999 m2) NEOM, KSA TIME: June 2023- August 2023 PROJECT ROLE: Junior Urban Designer Master plan Massing Study, Facade pattern study, 3D modelling, Photo-realistic Site plans ‘MIRAGE’ PRE CONCEPT DESIGN Pre-concept vision for a self-sufficient remote resort in KSA. Set within a secluded sabkha salt-flat surrounded by monumental dunes, the project reimagines the legendary lost city of Iram as a contemporary destination where myth, habitat, and future hospitality converge. Inspired by ancient narratives of carved cities and desert paradises, two master plan visions reinterpret Iram as a rediscovered civilisation shaped by landscape, integrating multi-segment accommodation, year-round entertainment, and adventurous experiences through climate-responsive and pragmatic design strategies.

31.text: Erum of the Pillars is a legendary lost city referenced in Islamic literature and Arab mythology, described as a powerful and wealthy oasis settlement in the heart of the desert. Passed down through oral tradition for millennia and first recorded in the early centuries CE, Erum is imagined as a grand city of towering pillars, lush gardens, and ornate architecture. Though no archaeological evidence confirms its existence, the legend speaks of an advanced civilisation— the Ad people—renowned for constructing monumental columns that symbolised the city’s power, prosperity, and mastery of the desert landscape. BRIEF - SHORT HISTORY OF IRAM OF THE PILLARS QUOTES ON ERUM OF THE PILLARS “The ruins of Iram of the Pillars lie buried beneath the sands of the desert, waiting to be rediscovered by intrepid explorers.” - Richard Francis Burton (British explorer, writer, scholar) “Iram of the Pillars was a marvel of human ingenuity and ambition, a city that rose from the sands and challenged the heavens.” - Jorge Luis Borges (Argentine writer, poet) “The legend of Iram of the Pillars is a tale of a prosperous civilization that was brought to ruin by the wrath of the gods.” - Paulo Coelho (Brazilian novelist) “The legend of Iram of the Pillars is a testament to the human spirit and the drive to create, even in the face of great adversity.” - Ibn Arabi (Scholar, mystic, poet, philosopher) “Iram of the Pillars is a symbol of the transience of human glory and the inevitability of our own mortality.” - Karen Armstrong (British author) “The lost city of Iram of the Pillars is a mystery that has fascinated scholars and adventurers for centuries.” - Tahir Shah (British author, journalist, documentary maker) true and fortunes were made.” - Anonymous LEGEND OF ERUM OF THE PILLARS REDISCOVERED AS A UNIQUE HOSPITALITY ‘CITY’ ARCHITECTURAL GRANDIOSITY ICONIC BUILDINGS UNIQUE CITY LAYOUT PROTECTED BY WALLS OR NATURE WATER VEGETATION VERNACULARITY The illustrative depiction of the mythical cities, lost cities and Erum share several common elements.

A terraced landscape spine guides guests from arrival through layered amenity spaces down to the shoreline, creating a gradual unfolding of views and experiences. As Landscape Design Lead, I led the concept and development of the terraced landscape framework, integrating pools, decks, and native coastal planting to blur the boundary between architecture and landscape while framing expansive views of the Red Sea. 48.text: PROJECT TYPE: Graduate Individual Project SCALE: Medium (1,000 - 99,999 m2) LOCATION: London, UK TIME: Oct 2021- August 2022 MLA Landscape Architecture Bartlett School of Architecture University College London RE-IMAGINE "FUN PALACE" IN ABBEY MILL PUMPING STATION Pumping Heterotopia reimagines the future of Abbey Mill Pumping Station by transforming retiring critical infrastructure into a playful and educational public landscape. Inspired by Cedric Price’s The Fun Palace and the concept of heterotopia, the proposal embraces the site’s industrial identity rather than concealing it. The design explores a kinetic landscape powered by gravity, hydropower, natural ventilation, and human interaction. By harnessing the site’s existing infrastructure and natural forces, the proposal creates self-sustaining public spaces that merge engineering, ecology, and landscape architecture while challenging conventional perceptions of infrastructure. PUMPING HETEROTOPIA
